$comment: Accepted npm audit advisories. Every entry is a dated, reasoned decision;
scripts/audit-check.py fails on any high/critical advisory that is not
listed here, and also fails when a listed advisory no longer appears -- a
dead exception is removed, not left to rot.
Adding an entry is a security decision: record why the risk is acceptable,
not merely that a fix is unavailable.

accepted.reason: Stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs. Reached only through @prisma/client -> prisma -> @prisma/config, whose sole merge input is our own committed Prisma configuration; no attacker-controlled path exists. No fixed release on Prisma 7.10 -- npm's suggested fix is a downgrade to Prisma 6, a breaking stack change. See docs/knowledge/project-state.md.
accepted.recheck: When Prisma publishes a release that bumps deepmerge-ts to >=8.

accepted.reason: Auth plugin downgrade to mysql_clear_password: a hostile MySQL server can make the client send the password in plaintext. Reached only as a transitive dependency of @prisma/client -> prisma, which bundles a driver per supported database; mysql2 3.15.3 is installed but never loaded, because this project has a single PostgreSQL datasource and PostgreSQL is the only permitted database (persistence-conventions.md PC-1). The vulnerable handshake therefore never runs, and no configuration in current scope can reach it. Fixed in mysql2 >=3.22.0, which prisma 7.10 does not yet pin; npm's only offered fix is a downgrade to prisma 6.19.3, a breaking major change that contradicts architecture.md AD-1 (Prisma ORM 7).
accepted.recheck: When Prisma publishes a release pinning mysql2 >=3.22.0 -- or immediately, and as a blocker rather than a re-check, if any Story ever introduces a MySQL datasource, which would make this path live.
